idea.title: Our longest dragon runs into its own body although it knows it: find why and fix it (4 hitSelf deaths of 12+ longest in 6 games)
idea.hypothesis: Rule counts' new round-500 tallies (branch rulecounts-r500, 2026-09-26) found our team's longest dragon, 12+ long, dying by running into itself (hitSelf) 4 times in the 6 kept rule-count games of champion 2c79f81 (v0030), about a quarter of its deaths before r397 not counted as head-on; on every one its debug line showed body == len, so the bot knew its length; whether it knew each segment's tile is unconfirmed (compare its tracked body with the replay's body tiles on those turns), and so is whether a safe move existed. Replays and maps kept in ~/.bc-loop/replay-notes/hitself-2026-09-26/: 0001-gen_eval_188302895-aB (our side B; deaths at r96 length 34, r145 length 58, r335 length 39, against the champion) and 0000-gen_eval_188302894-aA (our side A; r171 length 12, against the breeder). First watch each death turn (tools/watch.py dragon/frames) and name the cause (e.g. a sprint step, a portal, a fold/merge move, a move chosen as the least bad, a tail that didn't move because it ate): reproduce the worst as a failing scenario test from the replay state, then fix that decision. If the cause is 'every move was fatal', say so with the board and stop: that belongs to I004's search. Count how many of our deaths of dragons 8+ are hitSelf in a logging copy over 12 fresh maps before and after the fix.
